content.jointProblem: Can site-specific statistical or one-class baselines detect unusual Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP behaviour without labelled attack training data, while providing understandable alerts within ProtoSense's device-resource limits? The first experiment would test transfer to BACnet and ArmaturaSec's deployment conditions using chronologically held-out client traffic and controlled bench scenarios, measuring operator-reviewed false alerts, scenario detection, explanation usefulness, and resource consumption rather than assuming published performance will transfer.

rationale.text: Kiss has directly relevant experience developing and calibrating unsupervised detectors for operational SCADA networks without labelled attack data.

sources.quote: The project developed threshold calibration procedures for detectors operating without labelled attack data

rationale.text: Her Modbus work provides a concrete starting point for site-specific baselines built from register values, request timing, and function-code sequences.

sources.quote: This paper describes the construction of per-register statistical baselines for Modbus/TCP traffic captured over six months on a live substation automation testbed.
For each register address, empirical distributions of inter-request intervals, payload values, and function code sequences were estimated

rationale.text: Her incremental modelling research addresses legitimate operational changes and includes an operator-acknowledgement mechanism, relevant to maintaining site baselines over time.

sources.quote: Concept drift induced by a planned process reconfiguration was detected as a persistent anomaly episode; a supervised reset mechanism based on operator acknowledgement was proposed

rationale.text: She has evaluated model compression and inference on constrained ARM hardware, providing relevant deployment experience rather than only offline modelling.

sources.quote: This paper evaluates the effect of weight quantisation (32-bit to 8-bit and 4-bit floating point) and structured pruning
A combined 8-bit quantised, 25%-pruned model achieved inference at 0.9 ms per 10-second window on an ARM Cortex-A7 target

rationale.text: Her group has controlled ICS evaluation infrastructure and practical experience with utility monitoring partners, supporting a bench-to-field validation programme.

sources.quote: The group operates a dedicated ICS testbed equipped with Siemens-compatible PLCs, Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators, and packet capture infrastructure for long-term dataset collection.
Kiss has collaborated with a regional energy distributor and a water utility as monitoring data partners on two funded projects

constraints.text: Training and operational threshold calibration must not depend on confirmed attack examples; archived traffic must be treated as unlabelled rather than guaranteed clean.

sources.quote: we have zero examples of malicious traffic
if they were compromised they would not know.

constraints.text: The scope must cover both Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP, with site-specific baselines rather than relying solely on public-dataset models.

sources.quote: ProtoSense: passive protocol inspection module for Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic
What we actually need is something that learns what normal looks like on a specific site

constraints.text: Operational acceptance must address nuisance alerts and plant-manager-readable explanations, not just aggregate detection metrics.

sources.quote: it flagged so many false positives in real deployments that clients started switching the alerts off.
We need a method that works with no attack examples and that we can explain to a plant manager in plain language.

constraints.text: Inference must run on the appliance and be integrated with the embedded Linux environment; the design must respect packet-forwarding latency, with actual hardware budgets established before implementation.

sources.quote: we have the hardware to run inference on-device
Embedded Linux (custom Yocto build)
to support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency.

constraints.text: The work plan must fit one to two part-time company engineers; access to archives, the hardware bench, and firmware requires an NDA.

sources.quote: We can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project
with access to our traffic archives, our hardware bench, and our existing firmware codebase under NDA.

constraints.text: Use of the research group's testbed requires a data-sharing agreement.

sources.quote: Her group's testbed capacity is available to industrial partners under a data-sharing agreement.

risks: The supplied research demonstrates Modbus, DNP3, and other protocol work, but not BACnet validation. BACnet features, operating modes, and controlled anomaly scenarios must be tested in the first experiment.

Published detector and embedded-runtime results come from different networks and hardware. They do not establish performance on ArmaturaSec's client sites or appliances; the first experiment must include site-held-out evaluation and target-device profiling.

Archives may contain undetected compromises or incomplete operating regimes. A learned baseline could normalise malicious behaviour, while seasonal changes or maintenance could generate excessive alerts.
Without confirmed operational attacks, field recall cannot be established from archives alone. Controlled bench scenarios provide bounded evidence, not proof of coverage against real adversaries.
Plain-language alert explanations are a company requirement, but their usability for plant managers is not demonstrated in the supplied material.

Researcher availability, project funding, delivery dates, and exact appliance specifications remain unknown. The planned late-2025 hardware release is not evidence that the security processor is currently available.
Limited company engineering time and unresolved client-data permissions could delay integration, traffic review, and field evaluation.
questions: What researcher and student effort is available, from what start date, and what budget, duration, milestones, and ownership terms can both parties commit to?
Which appliance will host the pilot, has the planned security processor shipped, and what CPU, RAM, storage, inference-runtime, traffic-rate, and latency limits apply?
Can client permissions support university access to captures and derived features under the proposed NDA and data-sharing agreement, and what retention or security restrictions apply?
How much Modbus and BACnet traffic is available per site, and do captures cover maintenance, seasonal operation, configuration changes, and known incidents?
Which BACnet services and device types must be supported, and can the joint team reproduce representative BACnet normal behaviour and safe anomaly scenarios on a bench?
What false-alert rate per site per day, detection delay, and resource overhead would make a pilot acceptable, and who will review ambiguous alerts?
Can the first experiment separate training, calibration, and evaluation chronologically, include previously unseen sites, and reserve controlled attack labels for evaluation rather than training?
Who will validate alert explanations with plant managers, and who will authorise baseline updates after legitimate changes so that adaptation does not silently absorb suspicious behaviour?
